sanskrit: raśmimantau mahātmānau dīptimantau mahābalau dadṛśāte kuruśreṣṭhau kālasūryāv ivoditau
english: Radiant and great-souled, blazing and of mighty strength, the two foremost of the Kurus were beheld, like twin suns of doom risen at once.

sanskrit: vyāghrāv iva susaṃrabdhau garjantāv iva toyadau jahṛṣāte mahābāhū siṃhau kesariṇāv iva
english: Furious as two tigers, roaring like rain-clouds, the mighty-armed pair bristled with delight like a pair of maned lions.

sanskrit: gajāv iva susaṃrabdhau jvalitāv iva pāvakau dadṛśus tau mahātmānau saśṛṅgāv iva parvatau
english: Enraged like two elephants, ablaze like two fires, those great-souled ones were beheld like two peaked mountains.

sanskrit: roṣāt prasphuramāṇoṣṭhau nirīkṣantau parasparam tau sametau mahātmānau gadāhastau narottamau
english: Their lips quivering with wrath, gazing upon each other, the two great-souled best of men came together, maces in hand.

sanskrit: ubhau paramasaṃhṛṣṭāv ubhau paramasaṃmatau sadaśvāv iva heṣantau bṛṃhantāv iva kuñjarau
english: Both supremely exultant, both held in highest honor, neighing like two fine stallions, trumpeting like two elephants—

sanskrit: vṛṣabhāv iva garjantau duryodhanavṛkodarau daityāv iva balonmattau rejatus tau narottamau
english: bellowing like two bulls, Duryodhana and Vṛkodara, drunk with strength like two Daityas, those best of men shone forth.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājann idam āha yudhiṣṭhiram sṛñjayaiḥ saha tiṣṭhantaṃ tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: Then, O king, Duryodhana spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira, who stood among the Sṛñjayas blazing like the sun:

sanskrit: idaṃ vyavasitaṃ yuddhaṃ mama bhīmasya cobhayoḥ upopaviṣṭāḥ paśyadhvaṃ vimardaṃ nṛpasattamāḥ
english: "This combat between us two, between Bhīma and myself, is resolved upon. Be seated, O best of kings, and watch the clash."

sanskrit: tataḥ samupaviṣṭaṃ tat sumahad rājamaṇḍalam virājamānaṃ dadṛśe divīvādityamaṇḍalam
english: Then that vast circle of kings, seated all around and resplendent, appeared like the orb of the sun shining in the sky.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye mahābāhuḥ śrīmān keśavapūrvajaḥ upaviṣṭo mahārāja pūjyamānaḥ samantataḥ
english: In their midst, O great king, the mighty-armed and glorious elder brother of Keśava sat, honored on every side.

sanskrit: śuśubhe rājamadhyastho nīlavāsāḥ sitaprabhaḥ nakṣatrair iva saṃpūrṇo vṛto niśi niśākaraḥ
english: Clad in dark blue and of fair radiance, set amid the kings, he shone like the full moon ringed by the stars at night.

sanskrit: tau tathā tu mahārāja gadāhastau durāsadau anyonyaṃ vāgbhir ugrābhis takṣamāṇau vyavasthitau
english: And so those two, O great king, maces in hand and hard to assail, stood facing each other, hewing one another with fierce words.

sanskrit: apriyāṇi tato 'nyonyam uktvā tau kurupuṃgavau udīkṣantau sthitau vīrau vṛtraśakrāv ivāhave
english: Having spoken bitter taunts to each other, those two bulls of the Kurus stood glaring, like Vṛtra and Śakra upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vāgyuddham abhavat tumulaṃ janamejaya yatra duḥkhānvito rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then arose a tumultuous war of words, O Janamejaya, whereupon the grief-stricken king Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke thus:

sanskrit: dhig astu khalu mānuṣyaṃ yasya niṣṭheyam īdṛśī ekādaśacamūbhartā yatra putro mamābhibhūḥ
english: "Fie indeed upon mortal life, whose end is such as this—where my son, master of eleven armies, was the overlord!"

sanskrit: ājñāpya sarvān nṛpatīn bhuktvā cemāṃ vasuṃdharām gadām ādāya vegena padātiḥ prasthito raṇam
english: "Having commanded all the kings and enjoyed this earth, taking up his mace he now sets out on foot, in haste, to battle."

sanskrit: bhūtvā hi jagato nātho hy anātha iva me sutaḥ gadām udyamya yo yāti kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: "Having been lord of the world, my son now goes forth like one bereft of a protector, mace raised aloft—what is this but the working of fate?"

sanskrit: aho duḥkhaṃ mahat prāptaṃ putreṇa mama saṃjaya evam uktvā sa duḥkhārto virarāma janādhipaḥ
english: "Ah, great is the sorrow my son has come to, Saṃjaya!" Having spoken thus, the lord of men, stricken with grief, fell silent.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa meghaninado harṣād vinadann iva govṛṣaḥ ājuhāva tataḥ pārthaṃ yuddhāya yudhi vīryavān
english: Saṃjaya said: With a voice like thunder, roaring in his joy like a great bull, the valiant one then summoned Pārtha to combat in the fray.

sanskrit: bhīmam āhvayamāne tu kururāje mahātmani prādurāsan sughorāṇi rūpāṇi vividhāny uta
english: As the great-souled king of the Kurus called forth Bhīma, manifold and most fearful portents appeared.

sanskrit: vavur vātāḥ sanirghātāḥ pāṃsuvarṣaṃ papāta ca babhūvuś ca diśaḥ sarvās timireṇa samāvṛtāḥ
english: Winds blew with crashing thunderbolts, a rain of dust fell down, and all the quarters became veiled in darkness.

sanskrit: mahāsvanāḥ sanirghātās tumulā romaharṣaṇāḥ petus tatholkāḥ śataśaḥ sphoṭayantyo nabhastalam
english: Loud-roaring, thunderous, tumultuous, and hair-raising, meteors then fell by the hundreds, splitting open the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: rāhuś cāgrasad ādityam aparvaṇi viśāṃ pate cakampe ca mahākampaṃ pṛthivī savanadrumā
english: And Rāhu swallowed the sun though it was no eclipse-time, O lord of peoples, and the earth with its forests and trees shook with a mighty trembling.

sanskrit: rūkṣāś ca vātāḥ pravavur nīcaiḥ śarkaravarṣiṇaḥ girīṇāṃ śikharāṇy eva nyapatanta mahītale
english: Harsh winds blew low, raining down gravel, and the very peaks of mountains crashed down upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: mṛgā bahuvidhākārāḥ saṃpatanti diśo daśa dīptāḥ śivāś cāpy anadan ghorarūpāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
english: Beasts of manifold forms came rushing from the ten directions, and blazing jackals of dreadful aspect, most terrible, set up their howling.

sanskrit: nirghātāś ca mahāghorā babhūvū romaharṣaṇāḥ dīptāyāṃ diśi rājendra mṛgāś cāśubhavādinaḥ
english: Most fearful, hair-raising thunder-crashes resounded, and in the blazing quarter, O lord of kings, beasts cried out their ill-boding cries.

sanskrit: udapānagatāś cāpo vyavardhanta samantataḥ aśarīrā mahānādāḥ śrūyante sma tadā nṛpa
english: The waters in the wells swelled up on every side, and great bodiless voices were heard then, O king.

sanskrit: evamādīni dṛṣṭvātha nimittāni vṛkodaraḥ uvāca bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Having beheld these and like portents, Vṛkodara spoke to his eldest brother, Yudhiṣṭhira the King of Righteousness:

sanskrit: naiṣa śakto raṇe jetuṃ mandātmā māṃ suyodhanaḥ adya krodhaṃ vimokṣyāmi nigūḍhaṃ hṛdaye ciram suyodhane kauravendre khāṇḍave pāvako yathā
english: "This dull-witted Suyodhana cannot vanquish me in battle. Today I shall loose upon Suyodhana, lord of the Kauravas, the wrath long hidden in my heart—as the fire upon the Khāṇḍava forest."

sanskrit: śalyam adyoddhariṣyāmi tava pāṇḍava hṛcchayam nihatya gadayā pāpam imaṃ kurukulādhamam
english: "This day, O Pāṇḍava, I shall draw out the dart lodged in your heart, slaying with my mace this wicked one, the basest of the Kuru line."

sanskrit: adya kīrtimayīṃ mālāṃ pratimokṣyāmy ahaṃ tvayi hatvemaṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ gadayā raṇamūrdhani
english: "This day I shall fasten a garland woven of glory upon you, when I have slain this doer of evil deeds with my mace at the forefront of battle."

sanskrit: adyāsya śatadhā dehaṃ bhinadmi gadayānayā nāyaṃ praveṣṭā nagaraṃ punar vāraṇasāhvayam
english: "This day I shall shatter his body into a hundred pieces with this mace; never again shall he enter the city called Vāraṇasāhvaya."

sanskrit: sarpotsargasya śayane viṣadānasya bhojane pramāṇakoṭyāṃ pātasya dāhasya jatuveśmani
english: "For the loosing of serpents upon my bed, for the giving of poison in my food, for the hurling down at Pramāṇakoṭi, for the burning in the house of lac;"

sanskrit: sabhāyām avahāsasya sarvasvaharaṇasya ca varṣam ajñātavāsasya vanavāsasya cānagha
english: "for the mockery in the assembly-hall, for the seizing of all our wealth, for the year spent in hidden exile and the years dwelt in the forest, O sinless one—"

sanskrit: adyāntam eṣāṃ duḥkhānāṃ gantā bharatasattama ekāhnā vinihatyemaṃ bhaviṣyāmy ātmano 'nṛṇaḥ
english: "this day, O best of the Bhāratas, I shall reach the end of all these sorrows; slaying him in a single day, I shall be free of my debt to myself."

sanskrit: adyāyur dhārtarāṣṭrasya durmater akṛtātmanaḥ samāptaṃ bharataśreṣṭha mātāpitroś ca darśanam
english: "This day, O best of the Bhāratas, the life-span of the evil-minded, unrestrained son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is at an end—and the sight of his mother and father with it."

sanskrit: adyāyaṃ kururājasya śaṃtanoḥ kulapāṃsanaḥ prāṇāñ śriyaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tyaktvā śeṣyati bhūtale
english: "This day this disgrace of the line of the Kuru king Śaṃtanu, abandoning life and fortune and kingdom, shall lie stretched upon the ground."

sanskrit: rājā ca dhṛtarāṣṭro 'dya śrutvā putraṃ mayā hatam smariṣyaty aśubhaṃ karma yat tac chakunibuddhijam
english: "And King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, hearing this day that his son has been slain by me, will recall that inauspicious deed born of Śakuni's counsel."

sanskrit: ity uktvā rājaśārdūla gadām ādāya vīryavān avātiṣṭhata yuddhāya śakro vṛtram ivāhvayan
english: Having spoken thus, O tiger among kings, the valiant one took up his mace and stood ready for battle, like Śakra challenging Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tam udyatagadaṃ dṛṣṭvā kailāsam iva śṛṅgiṇam bhīmasenaḥ punaḥ kruddho duryodhanam uvāca ha
english: Seeing him with mace upraised, peaked like Mount Kailāsa, Bhīmasena, wrathful once more, spoke thus to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: rājñaś ca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya tathā tvam api cātmanaḥ smara tad duṣkṛtaṃ karma yad vṛttaṃ vāraṇāvate
english: "Call to mind, then, that evil deed of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra's, and of yourself as well—what was done at Vāraṇāvata."

sanskrit: draupadī ca parikliṣṭā sabhāyāṃ yad rajasvalā dyūte ca vañcito rājā yat tvayā saubalena ca
english: "And how Draupadī was tormented in the assembly-hall, though she was in her season; and how the king was cheated at dice by you and by the son of Subala."

sanskrit: vane duḥkhaṃ ca yat prāptam asmābhis tvatkṛtaṃ mahat virāṭanagare caiva yonyantaragatair iva tat sarvaṃ yātayāmy adya diṣṭyā dṛṣṭo 'si durmate
english: "And the great grief we suffered in the forest through your doing, and in the city of Virāṭa, as though we had entered the wombs of others—for all of that I take requital this day. By good fortune you are now in my sight, O evil-minded one!"

sanskrit: tvatkṛte 'sau hataḥ śete śaratalpe pratāpavān gāṅgeyo rathināṃ śreṣṭho nihato yājñaseninā
english: "Through your doing the majestic son of Gaṅgā, foremost of chariot-warriors, lies slain upon a bed of arrows, struck down by the son of Yajñasena."

sanskrit: hato droṇaś ca karṇaś ca tathā śalyaḥ pratāpavān vairāgner ādikartā ca śakuniḥ saubalo hataḥ
english: "Droṇa is slain, and Karṇa, and the majestic Śalya too; and Śakuni, son of Subala, the kindler of the fire of this enmity, lies slain."

sanskrit: prātikāmī tathā pāpo draupadyāḥ kleśakṛd dhataḥ bhrātaras te hatāḥ sarve śūrā vikrāntayodhinaḥ
english: "The wicked herald who wrought Draupadī's torment is slain; and all your brothers, heroes and valiant fighters, are slain."

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo nihatās tvatkṛte nṛpāḥ tvām adya nihaniṣyāmi gadayā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "These and many other kings have been slain because of you; and you too I shall slay this day with my mace—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: ity evam uccai rājendra bhāṣamāṇaṃ vṛkodaram uvāca vītabhī rājan putras te satyavikramaḥ
english: As Vṛkodara spoke thus aloud, O lord of kings, your son of unfailing prowess answered him without fear, O king:

sanskrit: kiṃ katthitena bahudhā yudhyasva tvaṃ vṛkodara adya te 'haṃ vineṣyāmi yuddhaśraddhāṃ kulādhama
english: "What use is all this boasting? Fight, Vṛkodara! This day I shall drive out of you your appetite for battle, O disgrace of your line!"

sanskrit: naiva duryodhanaḥ kṣudra kena cit tvadvidhena vai śakyas trāsayituṃ vācā yathānyaḥ prākṛto naraḥ
english: "Duryodhana, O base one, is not to be frightened with words by any of your sort, as some common man might be."

sanskrit: cirakālepsitaṃ diṣṭyā hṛdayastham idaṃ mama tvayā saha gadāyuddhaṃ tridaśair upapāditam
english: "By good fortune the gods have brought to pass this thing long desired and set in my heart—this mace-combat with you."

sanskrit: kiṃ vācā bahunoktena katthitena ca durmate vāṇī saṃpadyatām eṣā karmaṇā mā ciraṃ kṛthāḥ
english: "What use is much talk and boasting, O evil-minded one? Let this speech of yours be made good by deeds—do not delay any longer."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sarva evābhyapūjayan rājānaḥ somakāś caiva ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, all the kings and the Somakas who had gathered and were present there acclaimed him.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpūjitaḥ sarvaiḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ bhūyo dhīraṃ manaś cakre yuddhāya kurunandanaḥ
english: Then, honored by all, his body-hairs bristling with delight, the delight of the Kurus once more set his mind, resolute, upon battle.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva mātaṅgaṃ talatālair narādhipāḥ bhūyaḥ saṃharṣayāṃ cakrur duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: With clapping of palms the lords of men spurred on once more that wrathful Duryodhana, like a maddened elephant.

sanskrit: taṃ mahātmā mahātmānaṃ gadām udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ abhidudrāva vegena dhārtarāṣṭraṃ vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then the great-souled Pāṇḍava Vṛkodara, raising his mace, rushed with great speed upon the great-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: bṛṃhanti kuñjarās tatra hayā heṣanti cāsakṛt śastrāṇi cāpy adīpyanta pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaiṣiṇām
english: There the elephants trumpeted and the horses neighed again and again, and the weapons of the Pāṇḍavas, eager for victory, blazed forth.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaṃ tathāgatam pratyudyayāv adīnātmā vegena mahatā nadan
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Duryodhana, seeing Bhīmasena come on in this wise, undismayed in spirit, rushed to meet him with great speed, roaring aloud.

sanskrit: samāpetatur ānadya śṛṅgiṇau vṛṣabhāv iva mahānirghātaghoṣaś ca saṃprahāras tayor abhūt
english: Bellowing, the two closed upon each other like a pair of horned bulls, and their clash arose with the din of a great thunderbolt.

sanskrit: abhavac ca tayor yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam jigīṣator yudhānyonyam indraprahrādayor iva
english: And there arose between them a tumultuous, hair-raising combat, each seeking to vanquish the other in battle, like Indra and Prahrāda of old.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgau gadāhastau manasvinau dadṛśāte mahātmānau puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Their every limb drenched in blood, maces in hand, those resolute and great-souled ones appeared like two kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin mahāyuddhe vartamāne sudāruṇe khadyotasaṃghair iva khaṃ darśanīyaṃ vyarocata
english: As that great and most terrible combat went on, the field shone lovely to behold, as though the sky were thronged with fireflies.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin vartamāne saṃkule tumule bhṛśam ubhāv api pariśrāntau yudhyamānāv ariṃdamau
english: As that fierce and tumultuous melee raged on, both of those tamers of foes, fighting hard, grew weary.

sanskrit: tau muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya punar eva paraṃtapau abhyahārayatāṃ tatra saṃpragṛhya gade śubhe
english: Having rested for a moment, those two scorchers of foes, gripping fast their gleaming maces, once again fell to striking each other there.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryau samāśvastau nararṣabhau balinau vāraṇau yadvad vāśitārthe madotkaṭau
english: Beholding those two bulls among men of mighty valor, rested and rejoined, like two powerful elephants frenzied with rut for the sake of a cow-elephant—

sanskrit: apāravīryau saṃprekṣya pragṛhītagadāv ubhau vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmur devagandharvadānavāḥ
english: gazing upon those two of boundless valor, both with maces upraised, the gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas fell into utmost wonder.

sanskrit: pragṛhītagadau dṛṣṭvā duryodhanavṛkodarau saṃśayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vijaye samapadyata
english: Seeing Duryodhana and Vṛkodara with maces upraised, doubt arose in all beings as to which should win.

sanskrit: samāgamya tato bhūyo bhrātarau balināṃ varau anyonyasyāntaraprepsū pracakrāte 'ntaraṃ prati
english: Closing once more, those two kinsmen, the foremost of the strong, each seeking an opening in the other, maneuvered for an opening against the other.

sanskrit: yamadaṇḍopamāṃ gurvīm indrāśanim ivodyatām dadṛśuḥ prekṣakā rājan raudrīṃ viśasanīṃ gadām
english: The onlookers beheld, O king, the heavy mace, like the staff of Yama, raised on high like the thunderbolt of Indra—fierce and death-dealing.

sanskrit: āvidhyato gadāṃ tasya bhīmasenasya saṃyuge śabdaḥ sutumulo ghoro muhūrtaṃ samapadyata
english: As Bhīmasena whirled his mace in the encounter, a most tumultuous and dreadful sound arose for a moment.

sanskrit: āvidhyantam abhiprekṣya dhārtarāṣṭro 'tha pāṇḍavam gadām alaghuvegāṃ tāṃ vismitaḥ saṃbabhūva ha
english: Watching the Pāṇḍava as he whirled that mace of no slight force, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: caraṃś ca vividhān mārgān maṇḍalāni ca bhārata aśobhata tadā vīro bhūya eva vṛkodaraḥ
english: And weaving through manifold movements and circling figures, O Bhārata, the hero Vṛkodara then shone forth all the more.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya yat tāv anyonyarakṣaṇe mārjārāv iva bhakṣārthe tatakṣāte muhur muhuḥ
english: Closing with one another, each warding off the other, those two hacked away again and again, like two cats fighting over a morsel.

sanskrit: acarad bhīmasenas tu mārgān bahuvidhāṃs tathā maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi sthānāni vividhāni ca
english: And Bhīmasena ranged through movements of many kinds, and varied circlings, and stances of every sort.

sanskrit: gomūtrikāṇi citrāṇi gatapratyāgatāni ca parimokṣaṃ prahārāṇāṃ varjanaṃ paridhāvanam
english: the zigzag steps, the varied passes, the advance and retreat, the parrying of blows, the evasion, and the circling run;

sanskrit: abhidravaṇam ākṣepam avasthānaṃ savigraham parāvartanasaṃvartam avaplutam athāplutam upanyastam apanyastaṃ gadāyuddhaviśāradau
english: the charge, the feint, the firm stand with its grapple, the wheeling and the closing, the leap aside and the leap forward, the laying on of the mace and the drawing of it back—so skilled were the two in mace-combat.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau vicarantau tu nyaghnatāṃ vai parasparam vañcayantau punaś caiva ceratuḥ kurusattamau
english: Thus ranging about, those two best of the Kurus struck at each other, and feinting again, the two moved on.

sanskrit: vikrīḍantau subalinau maṇḍalāni praceratuḥ gadāhastau tatas tau tu maṇḍalāvasthitau balī
english: Disporting themselves, the two mighty ones wheeled through their circling figures; then those two strong ones, maces in hand, took their stand in the circle.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ rājan dhārtarāṣṭro 'bhyavartata savyaṃ tu maṇḍalaṃ tatra bhīmaseno 'bhyavartata
english: To the rightward circle, O king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra moved, while Bhīmasena there moved to the leftward circle.

sanskrit: tathā tu caratas tasya bhīmasya raṇamūrdhani duryodhano mahārāja pārśvadeśe 'bhyatāḍayat
english: And as Bhīma moved thus at the forefront of battle, Duryodhana, O great king, struck him upon the region of his flank.
